description: Tier 1 rule-based detection on CICFlowMeter flow records. Every threshold is here; change it here, not in code. Count thresholds are multiplied by the sensitivity factor (high sensitivity = lower thresholds = more alerts).

T1-PORTSCAN-01.description: One source probes many destination ports of one host inside a window, each probe carrying almost no data.

T1-DDOS-01.description: Several sources each flood the same destination service inside a window.
T1-DDOS-01.disabled_reason: No tested setting keeps benign false alarms at or below 1%: the best flags 6.71% of benign flows on held-out data (recall 0.8162, precision 0.5356). Enable only on a network whose busy services are known; the DoS rule still flags each flooding source individually.

T1-DOS-01.description: One source opens a sustained, high number of flows to one destination service inside a window. Name-service ports are excluded: many small queries to a resolver are normal, and DNS abuse is its own class.

T1-SLOWLORIS-01.description: One source holds many long, near-idle connections open to a web service at the same time.

T1-BRUTEFORCE-01.description: One source makes many connection attempts of similar size to an authentication service inside a window.

T1-C2-01.description: One source contacts the same destination service at regular intervals across the capture.

T1-EXFIL-01.description: A flow sends far more data out than it receives.

tuning.method: Thresholds chosen on flows in even-numbered minutes of TII-SSRC-23 and CSE-CIC-IDS2018 (02-20-2018), tested on flows in odd-numbered minutes.
tuning.selection: best F1 on the rule's own class with benign false alarms <= 1%
tuning.untuned_reason: no labelled attack flows with real addresses and timestamps for these classes
